clue.text: Instrument brought by tenor and bass on entering European city

parts.note: T is the standard abbreviation for tenor in music

indicators.note: the two short pieces go into the city's name, as one walks in through its gates

parts.note: Rome, capital of Italy
taken as written

explanation.surface: A musician arrives in a European capital with a tenor and a bass player, carrying an instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A trombone is a brass instrument played with a slide, so it is one example of an instrument.

clue.text: Current element in fashion provoking furious response

indicators.note: the unit sits inside the word for fashion

parts.note: a rage is a craze or fashion, as in 'all the rage'
the amp is the unit of electric current, an element of measuring it

explanation.surface: Something in current fashion stirs up an angry reaction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like 'present-day' beside 'fashion', but it is electric current, giving AMP.
explanation.definitionFit: A rampage is a spell of violent, angry behaviour, a wild reaction to provocation.

clue.text: Gosh! A lot of criticism is heading for major esoteric belief

parts.note: 'My!' is an exclamation of surprise, like 'Gosh!'

indicators.note: most of the word, with its final letter dropped

parts.note: stick is informal for harsh criticism, as in 'giving someone stick'
taken as written

indicators.note: the first letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: An exclamation at how much criticism is aimed at a major religious belief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criticism' is not fodder; it means STICK, and 'A lot of' trims it to STIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Mysticism is a belief in hidden spiritual truths reached through contemplation, which is esoteric by nature.

clue.text: Old American meat picked up in American city

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting the letters reads them from bottom to top

parts.note: ham is a cured meat

explanation.surface: An old American picks up some meat in an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' suggests a homophone, but in this down entry it turns AHAM upwards to MAHA.
explanation.definitionFit: Omaha is the largest city in Nebraska, in the United States.

clue.text: Half of couple blocking middle of scenery in Ravel?

indicators.note: the twin stands in the middle of those letters, getting in their way
the central letters of the word are kept, losing its outer letters

parts.note: one of a pair of twins is a twin, half of a matched couple

explanation.surface: Someone stands in the way of the scenery in a production of something by Ravel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle of scenery' gives ENE, the central three letters. 'Ravel' looks like the composer, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To ravel is to tangle or twist threads together, the same as entwining them; the question mark flags the verb hiding behind the composer.

clue.text: Physiologist father, very affectionate? Not half

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father

indicators.note: only half of the word survives, its first part

parts.note: loving means affectionate

explanation.surface: A scientist's father described as extremely affectionate, though only half so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half' looks like the slang for 'very much', but it keeps half of LOVING, giving LOV.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivan Pavlov was the Russian physiologist known for conditioning dogs to salivate at a bell.

clue.text: Variable item measuring the length of some text?

parts.note: para is short for paragraph, a section of text
a meter is a device that measures something

explanation.surface: A query about a tool that counts how long a piece of writing is.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as PARA-METER, a gadget for measuring a paragraph.
explanation.definitionFit: A parameter is a quantity in a calculation or system that can be set or varied, a variable.

clue.text: Who'd be foremost in various interesting church activities, right?

definitions.text: Who'd be foremost in various interesting church activities, right?

indicators.note: the leading letters of each of the following words are taken in turn

explanation.surface: A question about who leads a parish's many lively activities.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A vicar is the priest in charge of a parish, who would lead its church activities.

clue.text: Be around for longer than discarded cobbler's tool

parts.note: something thrown out is out
a last is the foot-shaped block a shoemaker works on

explanation.surface: Something lasting longer than an old shoemaker's tool that was thrown away.
explanation.definitionFit: To outlast someone is to survive or continue beyond them in time.

clue.text: Birds, a source of inspiration, appearing tail first

indicators.note: the last letter is moved round to the front of the word

parts.note: a muse inspires a poet or artist

explanation.surface: Birds inspire an artist, appearing rear end first.
explanation.definitionFit: Emus are large flightless Australian birds.

clue.text: Fuel active in the cart, pumped

parts.note: A is the grammatical abbreviation for active

indicators.note: pumped up, the letters are churned into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Fuel being pumped vigorously into a cart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pumped' rearranges IN THE CART into NTHRACITE.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthracite is a hard, slow-burning coal used as a fuel.

clue.text: Republican claims aid misdirected in reforming spirit

indicators.note: aid that is misdirected goes astray, so the letters go into a new order

explanation.surface: A Republican politician says aid has been sent to the wrong place in the name of reform.
explanation.definitionFit: Radicalism is a commitment to sweeping political change, the outlook of a reformer.

clue.text: King's dismissing good material

indicators.note: the letter is sent away from the word

parts.note: regal means belonging to or befitting a king

explanation.surface: A king rejects good fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'material' looks like a noun for cloth, but it is the adjective meaning physical.
explanation.definitionFit: Material things are physical and tangible, which is what real means here.

clue.text: Indifferent doctor keeping one sitting in pool

indicators.note: the whole group sits within the pool's letters

parts.note: a mere is a small lake or pool

indicators.note: the doctor holds the single letter inside

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A lacklustre doctor keeps a patient sitting in a pool.
explanation.definitionFit: Indifferent can mean neither good nor bad, only ordinary, which is mediocre.

clue.text: Understood opponents to be taking on honest Democrat

parts.note: cons are the arguments or people against, as in pros and cons
true means honest or faithful

explanation.surface: Political rivals were seen to take on a Democrat known for honesty.
explanation.definitionFit: Construed means interpreted, taken to mean something, so a word for understood.

clue.text: Fruit: cat taking most of a small amount

parts.note: a tom is a male cat

indicators.note: the word loses its last letter

parts.note: an atom is a tiny amount, as in 'not an atom of truth'

explanation.surface: A cat nibbles a little fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanically a tomato is a fruit, the berry of the tomato plant.

clue.text: Speech on gloom somehow upset international group

indicators.note: the letters fall into place in some unstated way
in a down entry, the letters are tipped over to read upwards

parts.note: the EU, the European Union

explanation.surface: A speech about gloom somehow upsets an international body.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram indicator rearranges ON GLOOM into MONOLOG; 'upset' turns EU into UE in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A monologue is a long speech by one person, as in a play.

clue.text: Independent critic's initial title recalled part of one of O'Neill's

indicators.note: only the first letter of the word is used
called back, so the word runs in reverse

parts.note: a title is a name

explanation.surface: An independent critic remembers a title from an O'Neill play.
explanation.walkthrough: Eugene O'Neill wrote 'The Iceman Cometh'; ICEMAN is part of that title.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iceman Cometh is one of Eugene O'Neill's plays, so the word is part of a title of his.

clue.text: English league spot initially seized by endlessly downmarket soccer club

indicators.note: those letters are grabbed and held inside the other word
the word loses its final letter

parts.note: cheap means low-grade or downmarket

indicators.note: the first letters of each of the three words are taken

explanation.surface: A top English league place is snatched by a tacky, cut-price football club.
explanation.walkthrough: CHEA (CHEAP endlessly) holds ELS. Chelsea is a London football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Chelsea is a Premier League football club based in west London.

clue.text: Warning new version of CSI about approach to court work?

parts.note: fore is the warning shouted on a golf course

indicators.note: a new version of the letters puts them in a different order

explanation.surface: A warning about a new version of the TV crime drama CSI.
explanation.walkthrough: 'version of' rearranges CSI into SIC. The definition is adjectival: forensic means relating to courts.
explanation.definitionFit: Forensic means relating to courts of law, now mostly scientific methods used in criminal investigation.

clue.text: Methodology applicable to most of Disney film

parts.note: for can mean intended for or applying to

indicators.note: the title loses its last letter

parts.note: Mulan is a Disney animated film

explanation.surface: A storytelling method that fits most Disney films.
explanation.definitionFit: A formula is a set method or recipe for doing something.

clue.text: Session in pub is resounding after start fails

parts.note: an inn is a pub

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word is lost

parts.note: sings means rings out or resounds

explanation.surface: A session in the pub gets noisy once a false start is overcome.
explanation.walkthrough: An innings is a team's or batter's turn at the crease in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: An innings is a period of play or a turn, a session at the wicket in cricket.

clue.text: Bridge team being eaten by opponents is source of headlines

indicators.note: the partnership is swallowed into the other pair's letters

parts.note: in bridge, North and South are the partners opposing East and West
East and West form a partnership at bridge

explanation.surface: A bridge pair loses badly to its rivals, which makes the headlines.
explanation.definitionFit: News is the report of events, the material that headlines are written about.

clue.text: Power in source exemplified in outer columns?

indicators.note: the letter is put inside the other word

parts.note: a seed is the source from which something grows
P is the abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: Power hidden in a source illustrated in some outside pillars.
explanation.walkthrough: The grid's first column reads TERMINAL and its last VELOCITY: terminal velocity is the top speed a falling object reaches.
explanation.definitionFit: Terminal velocity, spelt down the grid's outer columns, is a kind of speed, so it exemplifies the answer.

clue.text: Cake turned bad when packing in pasta

parts.note: a torte is a rich cake

indicators.note: the letters are turned round to read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
ill means bad, as in ill effects

explanation.surface: A cake goes off when stuffed with pasta.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses the whole of IN plus ILL, so the reversal gives LLINI, not two separately reversed pieces; 'when packing' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Tortellini are small ring-shaped stuffed pasta parcels.

clue.text: Positive reception elevated story about Cuba

indicators.note: in a down entry, raised up so it reads from the bottom
the story goes round the letter for Cuba

parts.note: a tale is a story
C is Cuba's international vehicle registration code

explanation.surface: A lofty story about Cuba is well received.
explanation.walkthrough: TALE round C gives TALCE; 'elevated' turns it upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Eclat is brilliant success or acclaim, a warmly enthusiastic reception.

clue.text: University engaged in a second reading, following normal practice

indicators.note: the letter is engaged, or occupied, within the word for reading

parts.note: perusal is a reading or examination of something

explanation.surface: A university student busy with a second read-through, as normal.
explanation.definitionFit: As per usual is an idiom meaning in the customary way, as always.

clue.text: Lowdown rat, ultimately, or courteous fellow?

parts.note: gen is British slang for information, the lowdown

indicators.note: the final letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: Is he a lowdown rat after all, or a polite chap?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lowdown' looks like an adjective for the rat, but it is the noun meaning information.
explanation.definitionFit: A gent is short for gentleman, a man of good manners.

clue.text: Arrived with lots of property

definitions.meaning: ... means owning land, as in the ... gentry

explanation.surface: A newcomer arrives owning plenty of property.
explanation.definitionFit: Landed as a past tense means arrived; as an adjective it means owning estates.

clue.text: A colt with a mane is theatrical

parts.note: C is an abbreviation for colt in horse-racing form guides
tressy means having long tresses of hair, like a mane

explanation.surface: A young horse with a flowing mane is very dramatic.
explanation.definitionFit: Actressy describes showy, affected behaviour, like an actress being dramatic.
